passage.ro: Hi Laura, Thanks for your email! I have never been to Scotland, but I would love to visit it one day. You asked about my town, so here is some news. I live in Sibiu, a beautiful city in Transylvania. I have lived here since I was born, and I have never thought of moving. There are lots of old buildings in the centre and many cafés where people meet on Saturdays. Last week I went to a concert in the main square with my cousins. It was free, and the music was great. I should study for my English test tomorrow, so I must stop now. Please write soon and send me some photos of your school! Best wishes, Mihai

passage.ro: Our school has started a recycling project this year, and it has already changed a lot of things. There are now three coloured bins in every classroom: one for paper, one for plastic and one for glass. At first, many pupils forgot to use them, so the class captains made posters to remind everybody. Last month the school collected over two hundred kilos of paper! The money from selling it has bought new books for the library. Mrs Dumitru, the science teacher, says that we should also bring our own bottles to school, because plastic is bad for the environment. Some pupils think the project is too much work, but most of us have become more careful. Next year we are going to plant trees in the school yard.

passage.ro: I have always liked eating, but I have never been good at cooking. Last month my grandfather decided to teach me. He says that every young person should know how to make at least three dishes. We started with an omelette. I broke two eggs on the floor, but my grandfather only laughed. Then we made a vegetable soup. I have made it four times since then, and it gets better every time. Yesterday I cooked dinner for my parents for the first time. They said it was delicious, although I think I put too much salt in it. Next weekend I am going to try a chocolate cake. I hope that I won't burn it!

passage.ro: On Tuesday I lost my phone on the bus. I realised it when I got home, and I felt terrible because all my photos and phone numbers were on it. My dad suggested that I call the bus company, so I phoned them immediately. A friendly woman said that nobody had brought a phone to the office yet, but she promised to call me if somebody found it. For two days I heard nothing, and I thought I would never see my phone again. Then, on Thursday afternoon, the woman rang. A girl had found the phone under a seat and had taken it to the office. I went there straight away and thanked the girl with a big box of chocolates. Now I never leave my phone in my pocket.

passage.ro: Doctors say that teenagers should sleep for at least eight hours every night, but many of us go to bed too late. My friend Radu used to stay up until midnight playing computer games. He was always tired in class, and his marks became worse. Last spring his mother talked to him, and he agreed to try a new routine. Now he turns off his computer at nine o'clock and reads for half an hour before bed. He has also started to ride his bike to school instead of going by bus. After two months, he says that he feels much better and he has more energy for football. His marks have improved too. Maybe we should all follow his example!
